newsitem.title: UK: UK phone watchdog paves way for number portability.
newsitem.headline: UK phone watchdog paves way for number portability.

text.p: Oftel, the British telecommunications watchdog, on Wednesday paved the way for allowing telephone customers to move to a different operator without changing their existing telephone numbers.
Oftel director general Don Cruickshank published proposals to amend telecoms companies' licences so that they have to offer the service, dubbed "number portability", if another operator asks them to.

"Number portability eliminates the hassle of changing your phone number when changing operator. This allows consumers to take advantage of the increasing competition in the UK telecoms market," Cruickshank said.
The licence modifications will initially only be proposed for users of fixed line telephones. Cruickshank wants to publish further proposals to extend number portability to mobile phones in May.
Number portability is expected to eat further into the customer base of dominant telecoms group British Telecommunications Plc.
According to Oftel figures, BT still has a market share of over 80 percent despite competition from cable and mobile companies.

Planned licence changes are intended to take place for all lincencees at the same time. The formal consultation will last for four weeks with a further two weeks for further comments on initial responses, Oftel said in a statement.
